processing: Black tea flavoured with bergamot and with vanilla or cream flavouring, often with cornflower or mallow petals. The cream is a flavour; the tea contains no dairy unless stated.
harvest_season: Not tied to a harvest: as with other flavoured blends, the base tea is bought in and blended all year.
appearance_dry: Dark black leaf flecked with blue cornflower petals, sometimes with mallow or vanilla pieces.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish amber, typical of a medium black tea.
taste_profile: Expect the citrus of bergamot softened by a sweet, creamy note, over the plain body of black tea; how strong each is depends on the blender.

brewing.notes: Brew Western-style, as with other Earl Grey blends. Taste at three minutes; longer steeps bring out tannin over the flavouring.

vintage_note: Not sold by year or season, as is usual for flavoured blends: it is a shop blend sold year-round. Scented teas tend to lose aroma with time, so buy small amounts and use them while fragrant.
description:
Earl Grey Cream is Earl Grey with a soft vanilla layer added: black tea, bergamot and a vanilla or cream flavouring. Despite the name there is usually no dairy in it, and the blend is sold by many tea shops rather than coming from one place.

Petals of cornflower or mallow are mainly for looks. Some blenders go further, with white chocolate pieces, rose buds or a touch of lavender, so two teas sold under this name can be quite different.

In the cup you get bergamot first and a sweet, creamy finish. The best ones keep the citrus and tea in front, while the worst drift into dessert territory. Brew it like any Earl Grey and don't leave it too long, since the vanilla cannot hide a bitter steep.

Read the ingredients and judge by smell if you can. If you enjoy a London Fog, this blend does some of the vanilla work for you, so go easy on any added syrup.
history: Little is documented about where or when this variation first appeared. It sits among the many modern flavoured variations on Earl Grey and is known today as a style name used by tea sellers, without a recorded creator.
